newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl's potential challenger woos U.S. businesses.
newsitem.headline: Kohl's potential challenger woos U.S. businesses.

text.p: The Social Democratic (SPD) politician most likely to challenge veteran Chancellor Helmut Kohl in Germany's general election next year left on Tuesday for a 12-day visit to the United States.
Gerhard Schroeder, premier of Lower Saxony state, the home of car maker Volkswagen AG, will meet high-level U.S. business leaders in a trip aimed at highlighting his economic competence.

He will spend nearly two weeks visiting U.S. industry leaders such as Microsoft chairman Bill Gates, Hewlett Packard chief executive Louis Platt, General Motors chairman John Smith and Dow Chemical chief executive officer William Stavropoulos.
The 53-year-old opposition gadfly, a former left-wing student leader who now has close industry ties, misses no opportunity to be photographed smoking a fat cigar.
His trip seems aimed at making an impression on business leaders in the U.S. that could rub off at home, analysts said.

As Germany suffers record unemployment levels and corporate investment slows to a trickle, Schroeder's trump card in next year's election campaign could be the broad support he is thought to have among business leaders, they said.

The Social Democrats have rejected pressure to choose their candidate before April, after Lower Saxony state elections. SPD chairman Oskar Lafontaine is also angling for the nomination but Schroeder leads the popularity polls by a wide margin.

Asked in a recent opinion poll who was best suited to tackle Germany's problems, Schroeder came out in front with 31 percent, ahead of Kohl, who won just 25 percent, and leaving Lafontaine an also-ran with a meagre 16 percent.

During his trip to the United States, which will take him from San Francisco to Chicago, Detroit and New York, Schroeder will also meet the heads of investment banks J.P. Morgan and Goldman Sachs and pay a visit to the New York Stock Exchange.

In Detroit he will seek to heal the wounds of a drawn-out battle between GM and Volkswagen, while in New York he will lobby hard for U.S. investment in Germany and give a speech on "Economic Perspectives" at an event hosted by the American Council on Germany and Norddeutsche Landesbank.

Travelling with him are industry representatives from his home state including Hubertus von Gruenberg, head of tyre maker Continental AG, Karl-Heinz Voss, the European head of software group Baan Company and Reinhard Volk, the managing director of EXPO 2000.
